Article Title: WhatsApp clue, Mygate trail helped CBI crack NEET paper leak
Article Text:
Kulkarni was engaged as a subject expert (chemistry) by NTA for NEET-UG 2026 - the medical entrance exam being cancelled on May 3 due to a paper leak.

Trail Led CBI To Students And Question Setters

NEW DELHI: A seemingly innocuous WhatsApp message from a parent asking chemistry professor PV Kulkarni for his address to gift him a watch rang the first alarm-bells for CBI sleuths probing the NEET-UG paper leak. What followed was a scan of an access control app used in residential societies (Mygate) and analysis of a WhatsApp group named 'Fifa world cup', which helped the agency trace the students who bought papers and ultimately the question setters who leaked them.The chargesheet filed by CBI revealed that Mygate app logs confirmed the presence of students in the apartment of the arrested accused Kulkarni. The logs matched mobile logs, corroborating their location.Kulkarni was engaged as a subject expert (chemistry) by NTA for NEET-UG 2026 - the medical entrance exam being cancelled on May 3 due to a paper leak. The test was reconducted on June 21.Though sworn to secrecy, Kulkarni chose to share questions with students who paid to attend "special classes" he conducted in his apartment just before the exam, the agency said in the chargesheet.His greed put paid to measures that NTA had taken to plug vulnerabilities in the logistics chain that were exploited by an organised gang.The testing agency had not factored in the possibility of subversion by a subject expert."Kulkarni and other accused paper setters would memorise or mark in a book the questions that were being set at NTA's office, later note down those questions at a hotel, and then pass these on to other accused," CBI said.The handwritten notes matched the leaked question papers. Kulkarni's seized phone contained pre-exam leaked papers in circulation and contacts with candidates, parents and co-accused. The phone contained nine images of the chemistry question paper and answer slips matching NEET-UG papers.Kulkarni, CBI said, also created a Whatsapp group called "special class" on April 25. The money, in lieu of questions, was directly collected from parents of candidates by Kulkarni or sent through co-accused Manisha Waghmare, a beautician.Nine students attended Kulkarni's classes between April 25 and 27, officials privy to investigations said. Besides, three candidates attended special classes in Latur. Eight students, who joined the WhatsApp group created by Kulkarni, and his scouts have confirmed to CBI that the leaked paper was shared with them.Kulkarni even made an attempt to get the physics paper for students, but it was leaked by another paper setter, Manisha Havaldar. She was on NTA's panel to set the physics paper and also to translate the question paper from English to Marathi and vice versa. Despite an oath of confidentiality, she allegedly leaked physics questions to the mother of a candidate for Rs 25,000 at the insistence of another accused.Eight days before the exam, Havaldar had handwritten notes of the leaked paper on her phone. She dictated the leaked paper to accused Tejas Shah for further circulation. On April 14, Shah, a member of physics faculty and chief operating officer of Abhang Prabhu Medical Academy, noted down the leaked questions dictated by Havaldar.The leaked papers also reached Rajasthan. Four days ahead of the test, 11 sets of leaked question papers were transported in a black Hyundai Verna to Jhunjhunu. The chargesheet details revealed that Mangilal Biwal and Dinesh Biwal - Sikar-based family at the core of the leak - were carrying printed material spanning the complete exam syllabus, across physics, chemistry and biology.One of the receivers, Amit, kept Class X and XII marksheets of candidates as security, and they were assured they would only need to pay if more than 150 questions matched the actual paper, CBI said.Another accused, Shivraj Motegaonkar, managing partner of RCC coaching centre, circulated leaked question papers to students, claiming these would be the "most expected" paper appearing in the exam. The night before the NEET-UG exam, a PDF file containing the question paper was leaked to 40-50 hostel students of RCC coaching students, sleuths said.On May 3, after the exam, students appeared in a video where they claimed questions predicted by Motegaonkar actually appeared in the test. The "RCC MOCK test question paper" was the leaked question paper, CBI has found.
Article Summary: PV Kulkarni was engaged as a subject expert (chemistry) by NTA for NEET-UG 2026 - the medical entrance exam being cancelled on May 3 due to a paper leak. His greed put paid to measures that NTA had taken to plug vulnerabilities in the logistics chain.

Article Title: Police put up posters of Lashkar commander across J&K, declare Rs 15L reward
Article Text:
One held, SUV seized after bid to mow down cops in Ramban

Ramban Police seized an SUV after its driver allegedly tried to run over policemen manning a checkpoint on the Jammu-Srinagar national highway in Kunfer, Chanderkote, early Friday. One suspect was arrested, and a hunt for underway for two others on the run.



The police team signalled the vehicle to stop for a routine check around 3.52am. The SUV driver, however, ignored repeated signals and allegedly sped up in an apparent attempt to mow down the cops, a police spokesperson said. Sensing danger, Constable Rasal Chand fired three warning shots from his service rifle. That didn’t deter the driver, who managed to flee the spot with two associates.



Police registered an FIR at Chanderkote PS under relevant BNS sections and launched a probe. A joint team of the Army, Ramban Police, SOG, and CRPF launched a manhunt for the three suspects and arrested one of them, identified as Altaf Mohammad from Udhampur. The SUV was also seized.



No terror angle had emerged in the probe so far, a police spokesperson said. The investigation officer and district mobile forensic unit collected evidence from the scene. Further investigation was underway.
Article Summary: Ramban Police seized an SUV after its driver allegedly tried to run over policemen manning a checkpoint on the Jammu-Srinagar national highway. One suspect was arrested, and a hunt for underway for two others on the run. No terror angle had emerged in the probe so far, a police spokesperson said.

Article Title: Former Nestle CMD Suresh Narayanan says India Inc needs to shed the ‘elite’ tag
Article Text:
Former Nestle CMD Suresh Narayanan in his new book, 'Courage Under Fire', writes that in a crisis people follow those they trust.

For over four decades,

Suresh Narayanan

has navigated boardrooms, brand battles and one of

India Inc

's defining crises. In ‘

Courage Under Fire

’ (

Penguin Random House India

), the former Nestlé India chairman and managing director looks beyond business strategy to explore what truly shapes

leadership

.

In an exclusive chat with Lopamudra Ghatak, he argues that clarity matters more than charisma, challenges India's obsession with pedigree that’s causing companies to overlook leadership potential, and reflects candidly on the lessons of the

Maggi

crisis. He also explains why

Gen Z

's approach to work-life balance deserves respect rather than ridicule, and recalls how a woman boss taught him that empathy is one of the key traits to being a good leader.

Congratulations on your book. How did the idea to write 'Courage Under Fire' come to you?

In 'Courage Under Fire' you write that "great leadership is not about position; it’s about responsibility, authenticity, and the ability to inspire trust, when it matters". In an increasingly trust-deficit and information-surplus world, how does a leader earn trust? And how does an organisation make trust a part of its DNA?

'Performative' is the word that's often used today ...

mukhota

Trust is the real currency of leadership.(Image generated by AI)

This bring me to my next question: Can leadership be taught, or is it something people are simply born with?

Nestle India CMD Suresh Narayanan (File photo)

That's an interesting point about the 'charisma myth' that surrounds

leadership. You mention in the book about visiting Tier-2 and Tier3- colleges, and how students there are often more grateful, hungry and eager to learn. Do you think they make better leaders?

The 'tag' matters?

Why great leaders don't need charisma(Image generated by AI)

You have spent over four decades across big brands. Do you think India Inc has begun to move beyond that elitism?

The modern workplace has become very volatile, with geopolitics and global uncertainty adding new layers of complexity. What's your advice for leaders navigating crises?

What should I say? How should I behave? What tone should I set?

In hindsight, do you feel that your response to the Maggi crisis was appropriate? Looking back, is there anything you would have done differently?

In 'Courage Under Fire', you write about the emotional effect the loss of colleagues during the pandemic had on you. Do you think business leaders, particularly men, are becoming more comfortable showing their vulnerable side?

You also had a woman boss during your career. Did her leadership style differ from your male mentors?

Gen Z and the emerging Gen Alpha are reshaping workplace expectations as they place a premium on work-life balance, purpose and flexibility. How do you see that influencing India's workforce in the years ahead?

After a 40-year career in corporate India, I wanted to leave behind a few lessons that had served me well. They're not prescriptions, but perspectives shaped by the crises and difficult moments I have experienced.'Courage Under Fire' is more of a personal journey through those defining moments - that focuses on people, purpose, partnerships, values, behaviour and outcomes. I thought it would be of some use to a younger generation entering the workforce.I think you've hit the nail on the head! Trust is the most valuable currency - for an individual as much as for an organisation. It emerges when three streams converge at one point in time.The first is purpose. Every organisation, and every individual, needs a clear sense of purpose, something that guides decisions and actions.The second is values. What do you want to be known for? What principles define how you conduct yourself, especially in adverse situations?Purpose and values, in turn, lead to the third element: authenticity. Unfortunately, in today's digital world, authenticity often gives way to performance.We spend too much time embellishing, instead of being genuine.Correct. Leadership isn't about saying what you'll do, it's about doing what you say. That's the dilemma many leaders face. Do they wear a(mask) that projects one image while concealing another?In order to establish trust among people, there has to be a convergence between purpose, values and authenticity, and that leads to outcomes. Over time, those actions create credibility, and credibility becomes trust.Trust is built when purpose, values and authenticity consistently translate into action. Over time, those actions create credibility, and credibility becomes trust.I've also come to see vulnerability as a strength, not a weakness. When people know you're human, that you have strengths as well as limitations, they know what to expect from you. Predictability in values and behaviour is reassuring. What people fear most is unpredictability.Ultimately, trust isn't about being the most liked person in the room. In a crisis, organisations don't rely on the most loved people; they rely on the most trusted ones. If I'm liked but not trusted, I won't be asked to lead when it matters. Trust, more than popularity, is what carries an organisation through difficult times.Leadership, for long, has suffered from some myths. The first is the myth of charisma - that great leaders must have magnetic personalities. The second is that complex communication (by leadership) is somehow superior. The third is executive presence: the belief that a leader must be a larger-than-life figure at any gathering and dominate every room they enter. And the fourth is the idea that leaders should only display their strengths while hiding every flaw, angularities.I don't subscribe to any of those myths. Leadership can absolutely be taught because, at its core, leadership is an act of being human.You don't have to be charismatic; you have to be clear. You don't have to be complex; you have to be transparent in your communication. You don't need the loudest voice or the most commanding presence. Some of history's greatest political and business leaders inspired people far beyond the reach of their voices.But leadership doesn't develop in isolation. It blooms through the right mentors, timely nudges and experiences. Looking back, I benefited from teachers, parents, colleagues, relatives and even competitors who pushed me to exceed my own expectations. Those influences gradually built confidence, not just the confidence to lead others, but the confidence to manage myself first.One thing we need to do as a society is demystify elitism. We place far too much value on where someone studied, where they work, the company they built or the organisation they belong to — as though those labels alone define success and achievement.Exactly, the tag culture. I believe those days should be behind us. Look at ISRO. They might have their own travails but the fact is that most of the talent that comes there are not from the premier institutions in the country and yet they do premier and outstanding work and make us proud as a nation.The same is true of organisations that consciously recruit from Tier-2 cities and smaller towns. I often find students there to be remarkably humble, eager and determined. They are trying to prove themselves against a system that has long suggested only the elite succeed.As leaders, we have to move away from that entitlement mindset and create space for talent to flourish. India has extraordinary talent. Some young people may not be the most articulate when speaking in English but they are capable of hard work and possess grit, discipline and can deliver on their promise each and every time.That's what the country needs—not people who merely preach from the pulpit, but people who consistently deliver.I think as a country now we are mature enough to realise that we cannot be a developing country or hope to become a wealthy country one day on the crutches of elitism. I think elitism is a crutch that we have to get out of as quickly as possible.I think the kind of companies that I worked in - Unilever, Colgate-Palmolive and Nestle - they always prided themselves in a middle-class culture. Their leaders weren't chosen because they came from privileged backgrounds; they rose through competence, commitment, energy and hard workI use the term middle class in a positive sense because it symbolises humility, integrity, transparency, trust and a strong work ethic. This is what middle-class India is, and these are the values we strive to teach our children. When those values enter an organisation, they become a source of strength.I do think the growing recognition of talent from Tier-2 institutions and smaller towns is slowly weakening elitism. But there's still work to be done. Our education system and employers must create more opportunities for capable graduates from less celebrated institutions.Too many people still believe admission to a top college guarantees success. Life doesn't work that way. Success is usually about moving two steps forward, one step back, and repeating that journey with resilience and consistency.There are two principles that have guided me throughout my career.The first is simple: a crisis never arrives with a calling card. You have to remain alert at all times. Don't be caught sleeping at the wheel. Anticipate risks before they balloon into crises.The second is to manage yourself before you manage others. That's often overlooked. When a crisis hits, we immediately focus on facts, meetings and firefighting. But we spend far less time asking:In a crisis, everyone's anxiety levels are elevated. The leader's role is to remain calm, anchored in the organisation's purpose and values, and provide stability.That's often the difference between a crisis handled well and one handled badly. The outcome rarely depends only on strategy. More often, it depends on leadership—how clearly you communicate, how consistently you act and how much confidence you inspire.The first lesson, that a crisis doesn't come with a calling card, certainly applies in this case. In hindsight, we could have done better in terms of sensing the environment and knowing that something was brewing in parts of the country. If we had been able to address it more comprehensively, maybe we would have been able to manage the outcome a lot better.Secondly, one of the important issues in managing a crisis is to have a single point of contact communicating to the environment. One criticism we faced was that we were slow in communicating. Looking back, I believe we could have responded faster.I don't know whether the dial has shifted enough in India to say that with confidence. But I do believe people follow leaders who are authentic, humane and emotionally present — not those who remain distant and issue instructions from above.Professor George Kohlrieser at IMD Business School describes a leader as a "secure base." I find that idea deeply meaningful. Just as we turn to a parent in moments of uncertainty, employees should feel they have someone they can approach with their fears, concerns and aspirations, someone who will provide anchorage in a crisis.Vulnerability, to me, is a source of strength. It acknowledges that you're still learning and growing. That's not weakness, it's humanity.We've long been told that men don't cry. But they do. Suppressing emotion doesn't make you stronger; it makes it harder to empathise. And empathy is one of the most powerful qualities a leader can possess.Wan Ling, who headed Nestle Asia-Oceania-Africa, was one of the toughest leaders I worked with. She could be incredibly demanding, yet deeply compassionate.What struck me most was that every conversation with her began with family. With many of my male bosses, business came first and family last. With her it was always, “How is your family doing?”. Only then would we move on to tackle the toughest business crisis moments.One of her greatest strengths was her ability to read a room. She sensed what people were feeling before anyone uttered a word. Just as importantly, she had the ability to step back, consider various perspectives and avoid rushing into decisions. That balance of empathy and judgement made her an exceptional leader.I see it as a positive shift. The old belief that success demanded 80-hour work weeks came at a huge personal cost. You may have earned more, but you often missed out on family, friendships and life's important moments. There's little value in reaching 80 and regretting that you never spent enough time with your parents or your children. So I welcome this change.These youngsters are not work-shy. They simply want work to coexist with life, and I think that's a healthy aspiration. I only wish my generation had the courage to tell our bosses at seven in the evening that we were leaving to meet family or friends. Instead, we stayed back until the boss switched off the lights, as though commitment was measured by the last person to leave the office.That said, balance has to be calibrated. Every generation has something to learn from the other.What also strikes me about young professionals is that they're driven by experiences. They move from one challenge to another in search of learning and fulfillment. I would encourage them to embrace the challenge itself rather than becoming overly anxious about the outcome. Careers are rarely linear. If you focus on learning, growth and doing meaningful work, the outcomes usually take care of themselves.
Article Summary: Former Nestle India CMD Suresh Narayanan writes that in a crisis people follow those they trust. He argues that clarity matters more than charisma, challenges India's obsession with pedigree that’s causing companies to overlook leadership potential. He also explains why Gen Z deserves respect rather than ridicule.

Article Title: 'Who introduced them?' US senator says it's odd to see Justin Trudeau frolicking around Katy Perry; 'He used to be in charge of a whole country'
Article Text:
Alabama senator says it's odd to see Justin Trudeau frolicking around Katy Perry.

Justin Trudeau and Katy Perry were recently seen in France celebrating what is being termed as their first anniversary. A Republican senator (Alabama), Katie Britt, said it's kind of odd watching the celebrity couple frolicking because Justin Trudeau led a country. "It's like, he used to be in charge of a whole country, now we sort of see him frolic," she said."But like how did he get with Katy Perry? That's actually the question we should be getting to. Like, who introduced them? Obviously they didn't find each other on an app. You know? Like, how did that go down?" she asked.The former Canadian PM and Katy Perry were first spotted together in Montreal in July 2025. In October, they were seen aboard Perry's yacht off the coast of Santa Barbara, California. They were seen hugging and kissing. During New Year's, Katy Perry posted photos with Justin Trudeau and since then, it has been one outing after another for the couple. In January 2026, the couple made their high-profile public appearances in Davos. They were seen at Coachella and then the Tribeca Film Festival, and their latest has been a French vacation."They're both complete exhibitionists when they're together," National Examiner cited a source as saying."It's probably shocking for people who know Justin from his political days.""The problem is Katy travels with this enormous entourage wherever she goes, so people are constantly having to sit there and avert their eyes," the same report said.Katy Perry ended her relationship with Orlando Bloom in June 2025 a month before she was first seen with Trudeau. Perry and Bloom are parents to six-year-old daughter Daisy Bloom. Justin Trudeau and his ex-wife Sophie Gregoire divorced in 2023 after 18 years of marriage. They have three children: Xavier, Ella-Grace and Hadrien.Doing his 'boyfriend duty', Trudeau drew flak as he attended the opening match of the FIFA World Cup in Los Angeles and skipped Canada's match."There is a long history of political powers dating or even marrying celebrities, including Senator John W Warner and Elizabeth Taylor, Senator Cory Booker and Rosario Dawson, President Nicolas Sarkozy of France and the model Carla Bruni, and Trudeau’s own father, Pierre Trudeau, and Barbra Streisand, Kim Cattrall and Margot Kidder. In most cases, though, the celebrities enter the politician’s world, remaking themselves to fit," an NYT feature on Trudeau's rebranding as a boyfriend noted.
Article Summary: Justin Trudeau and Katy Perry were recently seen in France celebrating what is being termed as their first anniversary. A Republican senator (Alabama), Katie Britt, said it's kind of odd watching the celebrity couple frolicking because Justin Trudeau led a country. Britt: "It's like, he used to be in charge of a whole country, now we sort of see him frolic"

Article Title: 'Get Harshit Rana and Rinku Singh': Ashwin names Mumbai Indians' ideal Hardik Pandya trade
Article Text:
Hardik Pandya (PTI Photo)

Speculation over Hardik Pandya's future with the Mumbai Indians continues to grow, and former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin has weighed in with his own assessment of how a potential blockbuster IPL trade could unfold.Pandya's future has been the subject of intense discussion following another disappointing campaign for Mumbai Indians. Under his leadership, the franchise managed just one playoff appearance in three seasons, while the 2026 edition ended with the five-time champions finishing ninth in the 10-team table.Reports have linked both Chennai Super Kings and Kolkata Knight Riders with a possible move for the India all-rounder. Ashwin believes those two franchises are the frontrunners if Mumbai decide to part ways with their captain, but he also outlined the kind of deal he thinks the franchise should demand.Speaking on his Tamil YouTube channel, Ashwin said Mumbai Indians should only consider doing business with Kolkata Knight Riders if the deal significantly strengthens their own squad."Don't count out Hardik going to a franchise other than CSK or KKR. The talk is that CSK will give Dube and a pacer, while KKR will give away Cameron Green. What happens if Green decides to focus on the Ashes next year? If I were MI, I would accept a deal with KKR on only one condition: getting Harshit Rana and Rinku Singh in return. That is the only way MI gets stronger," Ashwin said.He also pointed out that Mumbai would have to consider not only what they receive in return, but also how much stronger a direct rival could become by signing Pandya."MI will also think about who between CSK and KKR gets stronger through the Hardik trade. If CSK give away Dube and one Indian pacer to get Hardik, they get strong but not invincible. However, if KKR get Hardik, they suddenly look very strong. KKR will become a lethal batting lineup with Hardik. These are teams with five, five and three titles, so MI have to think about how they can ensure one of these teams doesn't leapfrog them," he added.The discussion comes at a time when both franchises linked with Pandya are entering transition phases. Chennai Super Kings recently confirmed the departure of long-serving head coach Stephen Fleming after an 18-year stint, while Kolkata Knight Riders are preparing for life after Ajinkya Rahane's retirement.Pandya's own campaign in IPL 2026 did little to ease scrutiny over his performances. The all-rounder scored 206 runs and claimed four wickets in 10 matches as Mumbai endured one of their poorest seasons in recent years.The 32-year-old has not played competitive cricket since the conclusion of IPL 2026, further fuelling speculation over both his immediate playing future and whether he will continue with Mumbai Indians next season.
Article Summary: Pandya's future has been the subject of intense discussion following another disappointing campaign for Mumbai Indians. Ravichandran Ashwin believes Chennai Super Kings and Kolkata Knight Riders are the frontrunners if Mumbai decide to part ways with their captain. The former India spinner also outlined the kind of deal he thinks the franchise should demand.

Article Title: "He is a great example to all the other guys”: Andy Reid reveals Patrick Mahomes’ extreme rehab routine after knee injury
Article Text:
Andy Reid reveals Patrick Mahomes’ extreme rehab routine after knee injury(Getty)

Why did Andy Reid call Patrick Mahomes a great example for the Chiefs?

Andy Reid reveals Patrick Mahomes spent seven hours a day working inside the Kansas City Chiefs facility

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Patrick Mahomes spent the Kansas City Chiefs offseason inside the team facility, not on vacation. The quarterback dedicated himself to rehab after tearing the ACL and LCL in his left knee, and Andy Reid believes that commitment set the standard for the entire roster.At Chiefs training camp in St. Joseph, Missouri, Reid gave one of the clearest looks yet at how much work Mahomes put into his recovery. The head coach did not focus on statistics or championships. He focused on the daily grind that took place long before the regular season began.During an interview with CBS Sports reporter Evan Washburn at Kansas City Chiefs training camp, Andy Reid explained that Patrick Mahomes approached the recovery process with the same intensity he brings to games.“He just goes. He kept playing, he gets his rehab taken care of before and after practice, you know how he is, he’s all in,” Reid said during the CBS Sports interview.Reid then delivered the quote that became the biggest headline from the interview.“He’s a great example to all the other guys around him that, ‘I’m gonna do whatever I have to do to get myself on the field,’” Reid said.The head coach added that the organization closely monitored Mahomes throughout the recovery.The Chiefs worked with doctors and trainers every step of the way because they understood how competitive their quarterback is.“I’m gonna listen to the doctors, I’m gonna listen to the trainers,” Reid said while discussing the recovery plan and the importance of following medical guidance.Reid also said Mahomes “attacked every day” of the rehab process. That detail is crucial because the recovery did not involve occasional workouts. It became a daily routine built around treatment, strengthening exercises, mobility work and recovery sessions before and after practice.Inside the Chiefs building, players already know Mahomes as the franchise quarterback. Reid’s comments showed that he also views him as a leader whose habits influence younger players. The message from the coaching staff was simple: talent is important, but the work behind the scenes matters just as much.The most striking detail came when Reid described how Mahomes spent his offseason.“He didn’t go anywhere. Seven hours a day, he was there working... and it pays off for him,” Reid said during the training camp interview.According to Andy Reid, Patrick Mahomes stayed in Kansas City and built his schedule around recovery work. The rehab included treatment sessions, strengthening exercises, mobility drills and recovery work connected to practice.When Washburn asked whether he appreciated Mahomes’ toughness even more now, Reid brought up Travis Kelce “He had a good teacher with Kelce,” Reid joked. “Kelce was the first one to do it, and you gotta beat him over the head to get him off the football field.”Mahomes entered training camp with questions surrounding his mobility after the knee injury, but the early signs from camp have been encouraging. He has looked comfortable during practice and has moved well during team drills.For a quarterback with three Super Bowl titles, this offseason was not about highlights. Reid’s comments painted a simple picture: Patrick Mahomes stayed in Kansas City, showed up every day and treated rehab like a full-time job.
Article Summary: Andy Reid said Patrick Mahomes spent seven hours a day working inside the Kansas City Chiefs facility. Reid also said Mahomes “attacked every day” of the rehab process. Reid added that the organization closely monitored Mahomes throughout the recovery.

Article Title: R Praggnanandhaa wins maiden Saint Louis Rapid & Blitz title
Article Text:
R Praggnanandhaa

Strong finish in blitz section

Big boost in Grand Chess Tour standings

Indian Grandmaster R Praggnanandhaa won his first Saint Louis Rapid & Blitz title in impressive style, wrapping up the championship with one round still to play.The 20-year-old finished with 23.5 points, staying well ahead of Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov, who ended the event with 22 points.Praggnanandhaa entered the blitz section after narrowly winning the rapid event. He continued his good form, losing only one game in the blitz and collecting 11.5 points out of a possible 18.His consistent performances helped him comfortably secure the title.Sindarov finished second, while American Grandmaster Wesley So claimed third place with 20.5 points.The victory lifted Praggnanandhaa to second place in the overall Grand Chess Tour (GCT) standings.The result has significantly improved his chances of qualifying for the Grand Chess Tour Finals, which will be held later this year.He now needs another strong performance in the final tournament of the season, which will be played in the classical format.Praggnanandhaa also benefited from the withdrawal of France's Alireza Firouzja from the remaining Grand Chess Tour events.Firouzja pulled out because of scheduling issues, and as per tournament rules, all the points he had earned this season were removed from the overall standings.The final Grand Chess Tour event begins on Sunday and will be played under the classical format.A top-three finish there would further strengthen Praggnanandhaa's impressive season. Earlier this year, he also won the Norway Chess title after finishing ahead of world No. 1 Magnus Carlsen.R Praggnanandhaa (India) – 23.5 pointsJavokhir Sindarov (Uzbekistan) – 22 pointsWesley So (USA) – 20.5 pointsLevon Aronian (USA) – 19 pointsFabiano Caruana (USA) – 17 pointsLenier Dominguez Perez (USA) – 17 pointsJorden van Foreest (Netherlands) – 17 pointsAnish Giri (Netherlands) – 15.5 pointsVincent Keymer (Germany) – 14.5 pointsAwonder Liang (USA) – 14 points

SLC XI:

Every time a Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) XI batter hit a boundary, Mohammed Nilam made his presence felt at the Nondescripts Cricket Club (NCC) Ground. The Sri Lankan super fan was in the thick of things throughout the opening day of the three-day warm-up match between India and SLC XI."I remember we met in Delhi during the Test. That Rohit Sharma story of him coming to my home, I remember, my friend," he told TimesofIndia.com on the sidelines.It was a pleasant winter afternoon in December when almost every Indian cricketer, including Virat Kohli, KL Rahul and Ajinkya Rahane, stopped by to greet the cheerful Nilam. His love for Indian cricket remains unwavering, even though his heart beats for Sri Lanka. Dressed in an Indian cricket team training jersey, he cheered enthusiastically for the home side.Right behind him, a handful of NCC members were enjoying their weekend with juices flowing and the music was just loud enough to enhance the ambience. After a humid morning, the conditions became pleasant, making it a very watchable afternoon of cricket.Just like the Colombo weather, the Indian bowlers too found their length in the afternoon session, making the contest between bat and ball gripping.Kuldeep Yadav, in particular, competed with Nilam for the loudest cry in the middle. He had plenty of loud shouts while testing the middle order on a pitch that was hard work for the bowlers. From Mohammed Siraj to Prasidh Krishna, Gurnoor Brar, Ravindra Jadeja, Manav Suthar and Kuldeep, every bowler took time before finding their rhythm. Saransh Jain followed a similar script, becoming the seventh bowler used that day.Strangely, Auqib Nabi, who has joined the team as a replacement for the injured Jasprit Bumrah, didn't get an opportunity to roll his arm over and continued on drinks duty with the rest of the support staff and the net bowlers. The management didn't feel the need to give the J&K bowler a warm-up before the series, indicating the direction they are looking to explore for the upcoming two fixtures.There was rotation behind the stumps too. Rishabh Pant wore the big gloves when the day got underway. Later, Dhruv Jurel replaced him after patrolling a close-in position from the start of the day. It was a nice workout for the bowlers, who navigated the hot and humid afternoon before getting some respite from the gentle breeze in the closing couple of hours of play.The NCC facility, metres away from the venue that will host the second India-Sri Lanka Test later this month, remained mostly deserted for the three-day fixture. Just when India started picking wickets at regular intervals, the area around the members' cafe and the media desk became very busy. A handful of spectators eased onto the railing to watch the final few overs, and their proximity to the biggest names in world cricket kept their smartphones busy.The visitors were dealt a blow when Shubman Gill was ruled out for the day because of an impact injury to his right ring finger during India's practice on Thursday."Captain Shubman Gill sustained an impact injury to his right ring finger during India's practice on Thursday. As a precautionary measure, he will not take the field on Day 1 of the warm-up game against SLC XI. The BCCI Medical Team is monitoring his progress. KL Rahul will lead the team in Gill's absence," the BCCI said in an official statement before the day's play.The opening day of the fixture, where India didn't have an ideal start with their captain not taking the field, was all about volume. The bowlers, Kuldeep in particular, got much-needed overs under their belt and picked up two wickets. SLC XI posted 363 for 8 at stumps. For India, Manav Suthar (2/33), Ravindra Jadeja (2/64), Kuldeep Yadav (2/76) and Gurnoor Brar (1/49) shared the spoils.There was a bit of turn for the spinners as the day progressed, and it will make the second day more enticing when India bat. Cristiano Ronaldo and his long-time partner Georgina Rodriguez are reportedly set to get married in Madeira this weekend after being together for nearly a decade. Reports claim the couple have booked a cathedral in Funchal for the ceremony and the luxurious Savoy Palace hotel for the wedding reception. The event is expected to be one of the biggest celebrity weddings of the year.While close friends and family are expected to celebrate with the couple, several famous football personalities may not be on the guest list. Over the years, Ronaldo has had disagreements, public feuds, and competitive rivalries with players, coaches, and pundits. Here is a look at people from Ronaldo’s past and present who are widely considered unlikely to attend the wedding.Cristiano Ronaldo has enjoyed one of the greatest careers in football history. Along the way, he has built strong friendships but has also had several high-profile disputes.Former Manchester United teammate Wayne Rooney is one name that is unlikely to receive an invitation. Their relationship changed after the 2006 FIFA World Cup, when Ronaldo appealed for Rooney to be sent off during England’s match against Portugal. Years later, Rooney questioned Ronaldo’s return to Manchester United.Ronaldo responded by suggesting Rooney was critical because of jealousy and even joked that he looked better than his former teammate.Another famous name is Lionel Messi . Although the two legends have always respected each other’s achievements, they have spent almost two decades competing for football’s biggest honours. Their rivalry has defined an era, but they have never been close friends. With Messi winning more Ballon d’Or awards and lifting the FIFA World Cup, many believe he is unlikely to be part of Ronaldo’s wedding celebrations.Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag also appears unlikely to attend. Their relationship broke down during Ronaldo’s second spell at Old Trafford after disagreements over playing time. Ronaldo later said he had lost respect for the Dutch coach, and both sides eventually agreed to end his contract.Interim Manchester United manager Ralf Rangnick also had a difficult relationship with Ronaldo. Reports at the time suggested Ronaldo was unhappy with Rangnick’s tactical approach and questioned his appointment.Former England striker Gary Lineker has often said he believes Messi is the greatest footballer ever. According to Lineker, Ronaldo stopped following him on social media after those comments. Lineker later explained that he had simply shared his honest football opinion rather than trying to offend Ronaldo.Former Real Madrid forward Antonio Cassano repeatedly criticised Ronaldo during his Juventus years, describing him as an individual player who struggled to fit into a team system. Cassano later revealed that Ronaldo contacted him directly, highlighting his achievements and asking for greater respect.Former FIFA president Sepp Blatter completes the list. In 2013, Blatter jokingly suggested Ronaldo spent more time on his appearance than Messi. Ronaldo publicly shared the remarks, leading Blatter to apologise to both the Portuguese star and Real Madrid. Even so, the incident remains one of the most talked-about moments in their relationship.

Article Title: 'Replied with his bat': Shikhar Dhawan throws support behind Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli for 2027 World Cup
Article Text:
Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma

Former India opener Shikhar Dhawan has backed Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli to play in the 2027 ODI World Cup, saying the two will continue to add value to the Indian team and help it compete for the title.Now playing only ODI cricket, Rohit and Kohli had a productive series against England in July, despite India losing the three-match series 2-1.Questions have continued over whether 39-year-old Rohit and 37-year-old Kohli will be part of India's squad for the 2027 ODI World Cup because of their age. But both have continued to answer those doubts with their performances. Kohli scored two half-centuries in the series against England, while Rohit hit a century at Lord's.Speaking to news agency ANI, Dhawan said both Rohit and Kohli have been serving Indian cricket for many years and remain important to the team. He added that he has known both players since they were around 16 years old.Dhawan praised Rohit for bouncing back with a century at Lord's, saying the opener responded to a difficult phase with his bat and has been doing that throughout his career.He also praised Kohli's fitness and consistency, saying words are never enough to describe his achievements. Dhawan said he is confident that both players will continue to make a big contribution and help India in the 2027 World Cup."They are legends, they have performed for the country for so many years. Whether it's Virat or Rohit, all of us have had a relationship since we were around 16 years old. They are 2-3 years younger than me. And it's a matter of great joy that they are preparing now. Rohit recently scored a hundred at Lord's, so he scored a wonderful century and showed how his bat talks. Well, he's been showing it for so many years. And when a bit of a tough situation came, he replied with his bat," Dhawan said."And as for Virat, the more he is praised, the less it is. Keeping himself so fit, performing so well. And I'm sure that both of them will add a lot of value in the World Cup and help the team win," Dhawan added.
Article Summary: Former India opener Shikhar Dhawan has backed Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli to play in the 2027 ODI World Cup. Dhawan said both Rohit and Kohli have been serving Indian cricket for many years. He added that he has known both players since they were around 16 years old.

England white-ball head coach Brendon McCullum has thrown his weight behind the England and Wales Cricket Board's decision to hand Joe Root the Test captaincy once again, insisting Harry Brook 's opportunity to lead the side in the longest format will arrive in due course.The ECB's decision to bring Root back as Test captain after Ben Stokes' retirement came as a surprise, with many expecting vice-captain Brook to take over. Brook has already been leading England's white-ball sides and was widely regarded as the frontrunner to succeed Stokes.However, McCullum believes England have made the right call by opting for Root's experience while continuing to groom Brook for the future."Everyone knows the affection that I have for Harry," white-ball head coach McCullum told Sky Sports. "He's a wonderful player and he's doing a fine job as white-ball leader. I think his time will come in the Test job."McCullum said England would continue investing in Brook's leadership development, adding that the 27-year-old remains central to the team's long-term plans."I'm looking forward to working with him and hopefully growing and developing him into the leader that he can become.At some stage in the future, he will have a very important role in that capacity. But for now, Joe will do an amazing job," he added.Root's return marks a dramatic twist in England's leadership story. His first spell as Test captain ended amid mounting criticism before Ben Stokes replaced him, but following Stokes' retirement, the ECB has turned back to its most prolific Test batter to guide the side through a new era.The leadership reshuffle has also extended to the coaching setup. McCullum has stepped down as England's Test coach, with former Chennai Super Kings head coach Stephen Fleming taking charge of the red-ball side.McCullum believes England could not have found a better successor, describing Fleming as an outstanding appointment."I had a great time in my four years but now it's going in a different direction, I think Flem (Fleming) will be excellent. He's a little bit like me, but better – that's how I would sum him up. He'll do a great job, and the ECB have done incredibly well to get someone like him to commit to English cricket for the period that he has. It's an outstanding achievement," McCullum said.

Article Title: How Tkachuk family became hockey's most influential dynasty: Legacy Keith Tkachuk built and how Matthew Tkachuk and Brady Tkachuk took it to even greater NHL heights

The lasting legacy of the Tkachuk family in American hockey

Family Member Greatest Contributions Keith Tkachuk Hall of Fame career, 538 NHL goals, Team USA pioneer, established the family legacy Matthew Tkachuk Florida Panthers star, Stanley Cup champion, elite power forward, Team USA standout Brady Tkachuk Former Ottawa Senators captain, Florida Panthers forward, respected NHL leader Combined Legacy Multi-generational NHL excellence, leadership, championships and continued influence on American hockey

Few families in the United States have had as much of an impact on the modern game of hockey as the Tkachuk family. The family name has become synonymous with elite talent, fierce competitiveness and leadership over three generations of impact, starting with Keith Tkachuk and continuing with his sons Matthew Tkachuk and Brady Tkachuk. Their story isn’t just statistics or championships, but building a culture that blends ability with physicality, accountability and love for the game.Keith Tkachuk blazed a trail with an amazing 18-season NHL career that made him one of the greatest American-born power forwards in league history. The legacy has been lifted even higher by Matthew Tkachuk of the Florida Panthers and Brady Tkachuk, who followed his brother to Florida after making his mark as captain of the Ottawa Senators. The trio has helped redefine what American hockey players can do at the NHL and international levels.Keith Tkachuk was already one of the NHL's premier power forwards long before Matthew and Brady were household names. Big Walt, as he was known, added elite offensive production, toughness, consistency and leadership to an 18-season NHL career.Keith spent his entire career with the Winnipeg Jets, Phoenix Coyotes, St.Louis Blues and Atlanta Thrashers. In the 1996-97 season, he became the first American-born player to lead the NHL in goals, a sign of the growing influence of American players in a league long dominated by Canadian talent.Keith may not have done the most for hockey by scoring 538 goals, but rather by the environment he provided for Matthew and Brady growing up.Like many former professional athletes, Keith never put huge expectations on his children and always stressed the enjoyment of the game. Hockey was still something to get excited about, not something to press for, and it gave both sons a chance to develop naturally, while preserving their love for competition.Hell was to pay in the Tkachuk household. Whether playing hockey in the driveway, competing in backyard games or watching NHL contests together, each activity was a learning opportunity. Keith encouraged both boys to compete against each other but also respect their teammates and the opposition.Communication was also a defining strength of the family. Keith taught hockey IQ, preparation and accountability through everyday conversations, not long lectures. That showed later in Matthew’s emotional leadership and Brady’s ability to inspire teammates.Keith also made certain that his sons knew that talent alone would never guarantee success. Hard work, consistency and resilience were non-negotiable values throughout their development.Matt Tkachuk stepped onto the professional hockey scene loaded with expectations, as the son of one of the greatest NHL players in American history. Rather than getting bogged down in those comparisons, he quickly established himself as one of the league’s top power forwards.The Calgary Flames picked Matthew sixth overall in the 2016 NHL Draft, and he quickly showed the scoring touch, creativity and physical edge that had become synonymous with the Tkachuk name. Everything changed when he was traded to the Florida Panthers in 2022. Matthew quickly became the heart and soul of the Panthers, helping turn the franchise into a perennial Stanley Cup contender.While Matthew may have gotten to the NHL first, Brady Tkachuk quickly demonstrated that he possessed many of the same qualities that paved the way for his father and older brother’s success. Drafted fourth overall by the Ottawa Senators in the 2018 NHL Draft, Brady quickly established himself as one of the league’s most fearless young forwards.Those leadership qualities paid off in November 2021 when Brady was named the 10th captain in Ottawa Senators franchise history. Only 22 years old, he was handed the reins to guide one of the NHL’s youngest rosters through a tough time. His teammates often praised his consistency, accountability and desire to lead by example, not just talk.Brady’s offence just kept getting better, too. Multiple 30-goal seasons and career-best point totals made him more than just a physical forward. Brady, like his father and brother, proved that toughness and elite offensive talent could be found in the same player.His next trade to the Florida Panthers brought the Tkachuk brothers back together at the NHL level for one of hockey’s most compelling storylines. The two became teammates, fulfilling a childhood dream, and giving the Panthers two of the league’s most competitive power forwards on the same roster.There have been plenty of famous family names in pro hockey, but few have built a legacy quite like the Tkachuks. Their impact goes beyond championships, statistics or Hall of Fame recognition. The consistency with which they’ve embraced the same core values while adapting to different eras of the sport is what really separates each generation.Keith offered a physical play blueprint that did not compromise offensive excellence. While many enforcers didn’t offer much offensively, Keith was one of the NHL’s toughest competitors and always ranked among the league’s top scorers. Matthew and Brady built on those concepts, showing that a player with elite skill and relentless competitive fire can thrive even in the faster, more modern NHL.The Tkachuk family has become one of the defining stories of modern American hockey. Keith’s Hall of Fame career laid the groundwork, but Matthew and Brady have made sure the family name continues to grow with each passing season.Their successes have helped redefine the image of American-born NHL players. Past generations have had to fight the stereotypes that the European or Canadian players were better skilled, while the Americans were more athletic and physical. The Tkachuks have shown that elite offensive production, hockey IQ and toughness can all co-exist at the highest level.
Article Summary: The Tkachuk family is synonymous with elite talent, fierce competitiveness and leadership. The legacy has been lifted even higher by sons Matthew and Brady. The family name has become synonymous with NHL excellence, leadership, championships and continued influence on American hockey.

Article Title: Who is Sarah Jukaku? Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed has rental properties in India, Dubai in wife's name

Healing Politics: A Doctor's Journey into the Heart of Our Political Epidemic

The Michigan Daily

Article Title: Who was Sydney Towle? TikTok star who inspired millions while documenting her cancer journey dies at 26
Article Text:
TikTok creator Sydney Towle has died at 26 after a nearly three-year battle with cholangiocarcinoma, a rare bile duct cancer. Known for documenting her cancer journey with honesty and optimism, she inspired millions by promoting awareness and self-advocacy. Her family confirmed her passing, while fans and celebrities, including Alyssa Milano, paid heartfelt tributes. Towle's resilience, positivity and determination left a lasting impact on countless people around the world.

Who was Sydney Towle before TikTok knew her story?

The diagnosis that changed everything

Why Sydney Towle chose to share her cancer journey

The online criticism she faced

How her followers responded after her death

Why Sydney Towle's story resonated with young people

Sydney Towle spent nearly three years showing the internet what courage looked like. Even as an aggressive cancer reshaped her life, the 26-year-old creator refused to let it define her spirit. Her death has left millions grieving, but the messages pouring across social media make one thing clear. Her honesty, optimism and determination created a legacy that will outlive every viral video she ever posted.Before becoming a familiar face on TikTok, Sydney Towle was a young woman with big ambitions and an infectious personality. Living in New York City, she loved fashion, spending time with friends and documenting everyday moments that felt authentic rather than curated. Her content reflected joy long before cancer entered the picture.As her online audience grew to more than one million followers on TikTok and over 200,000 on Instagram, people connected with her openness and warm personality. Even after receiving a life-changing diagnosis, she continued to celebrate milestones.One of her proudest moments came when she fulfilled a longtime dream by walking the runway during The Chemo Club x Post Swim show at Miami Swim Week.It became a powerful reminder that illness did not erase her dreams.Towle was diagnosed with cholangiocarcinoma, a rare and aggressive bile duct cancer. Over time, the disease spread to other areas of her body, including her peritoneum, the membrane surrounding the abdominal and pelvic organs.She underwent years of chemotherapy and numerous treatments while documenting both the victories and setbacks. In May, she revealed that her oncologist had stopped treating her cancer and recommended end-of-life care. Rather than giving up, she sought another specialist and remained determined to keep fighting.Her family announced her passing in a heartfelt message."Syd went peacefully last night after an almost three-year-long battle with cholangiocarcinoma."They also honored the purpose she found through her platform."We are so proud of how hard Sydney fought and for sharing her journey with so many people. She wanted to raise awareness for rare cancers and was passionate about promoting self-advocacy. We will continue her legacy and honour her in every way we can."Towle never hid the difficult realities of cancer. She showed hospital stays, treatment days, emotional lows and joyful moments with equal honesty.She even embraced the scars left by treatment, including the hepatic artery pump implanted in her body. Instead of hiding it, she used it to encourage others struggling with body image and illness.Her social media often balanced painful updates with hope."Rich in life because my friends choose to spend a Saturday fundraising for cancer research."She also reminded followers to appreciate life's simple pleasures."Go get a pint of Ben and Jerry's, watch your favourite movie, remember that life is good and bad things happen sometimes but that doesn't make it a bad life."In another deeply personal reflection, she wrote:"I have only recently started seeing the resilience and beauty in this body. Scars that remind me of how far I've come. And I'm reminded that dreams only end when you allow them to."Being transparent online also exposed Towle to criticism. Some questioned her appearance, while others misunderstood why she continued posting during treatment.She rarely allowed negativity to shape her message. Instead, she focused on educating people about rare cancers, encouraging early medical attention and reminding others that every patient's experience is different. Her content remained centered on hope rather than conflict, earning admiration for its honesty and resilience.The announcement of Towle's death prompted an overwhelming response across social media. Thousands shared tributes celebrating the impact she had on their lives.Actress Alyssa Milano wrote:"Sweet angel. Fly high. Praying for all who loved her. She is really something special."Other followers echoed the same feelings."You were such a bright light and will be missed."Another tribute read:"How lucky we all are to have found you on the internet. Thank you for sharing yourself and your story."The messages reflected how deeply strangers had connected with someone they had never met in person.Sydney Towle's influence stretched beyond social media numbers. She gave young adults facing illness someone who understood their fears without pretending everything was perfect. She spoke honestly about pain while still making room for laughter, friendship and hope.Her videos became more than updates. They became reminders that resilience can exist alongside vulnerability. By sharing every chapter of her journey, Towle transformed personal hardship into a source of comfort for countless people, ensuring her voice will continue inspiring others long after her final post.
Article Summary: Sydney Towle was diagnosed with cholangiocarcinoma, a rare and aggressive bile duct cancer. Her death has left millions grieving, but the messages pouring across social media make one thing clear. Her honesty, optimism and determination created a legacy that will outlive every viral video.

Article Title: Meet Betty Bromage: 97-year-old breaks her own Guinness World Record as oldest female wing walker after recovering from stroke
Article Text:
Meet Betty Bromage: 97-year-old breaks her own Guinness World Record as oldest female wing walker after recovering from stroke

Wing walk comes after recovering from stroke

'I'd just get bored otherwise'

Inspired by a message from her nursing days

Already planning a challenge for her 100th birthday

At an age when most people slow down, 97-year-old Betty Bromage has once again taken to the skies, this time to break her own Guinness World Record as the oldest female wing walker.The Cheltenham resident completed the daring challenge by being strapped to the top of an aircraft as it flew through the sky, raising money for the stroke unit at Cheltenham General Hospital, where she received treatment after suffering a stroke in 2025.The feat marks Bromage's sixth wing walk, with her first completed at the age of 87. She had previously set the Guinness World Record four years ago and has now reclaimed the title by surpassing her own achievement.Bromage suffered a stroke in 2025, which continues to affect her speech, but she said she was determined not to let it stop her from doing what she loves."They treated me so well," she told BCC, referring to the hospital staff who cared for her. "It affects my words, but the rest of me is fine."Her latest wing walk was organised to raise funds for the hospital's stroke unit as a way of thanking the medical team that helped her during her recovery.According to the hospital's charity, donations from the fundraiser will help purchase equipment that will benefit both patients and healthcare staff.Despite approaching her 100th birthday, Bromage says she has no plans to give up adventurous challenges."I'd just get bored of life otherwise," she said. "I can't drive, I can't see very well and I get a bit frustrated. So, I want to do the things I can do."Known for her fearless spirit, Bromage joked that the most difficult part of wing walking isn't flying through the air, it's climbing onto the aircraft."The only problem is getting up on the wing because I'm quite short. Once you're up there, no problem. The fairground is a lot worse," she said with a laugh.A former nurse, Bromage said her passion for fundraising was inspired by a quote she once saw displayed on a hospital wall."We pass through this world but once. Any good we can do, any kindness we can show, do it now. Do not defer or neglect it. You will not pass this way again," she recalled.She said those words have stayed with her throughout her life and continue to motivate her charitable work.Hospital charity representative Imogen Sims praised Bromage's extraordinary determination, saying staff were grateful for her support."To take on such a daring challenge to support our team is amazing," Sims said, adding that the funds raised would make a real difference for patients and staff alike.As for what's next, Bromage is already thinking ahead."I'll have to think of something when I'm 100," she said. "Something special."Her latest record-breaking wing walk has once again proven that age is no barrier to adventure, or to giving back to the community.
Article Summary: Betty Bromage, 97, breaks her own Guinness World Record as oldest female wing walker. Cheltenham resident completed the challenge by being strapped to the top of an aircraft as it flew through the sky. Bromage suffered a stroke in 2025, which continues to affect her speech, but she said she was determined not to let it stop her from doing what she loves.

Article Title: Marathi literary luminary Shrinivas Kulkarni passes away at 92
Article Text:
Writer, editor Shrinivas Kulkarni

Kolhapur

:





Renowned Marathi prose writer and essayist Shrinivas Vinayak Kulkarni, popularly known as ‘Shrivi’, passed away at Karad on Thursday following a prolonged illness. He was 92.Kulkarni, considered one of the most distinctive voices in Marathi prose, is survived by his wife, two sons, daughters-in-law and grandchildren. His last rites were performed in Karad on Thursday evening in the presence of family members and members of the literary fraternity.Widely acclaimed for his landmark work ‘Doh’, Kulkarni brought to life the landscape, people and memories of Audumbar, his village in Sangli district, on the banks of Krishna river.Paying tribute to his literary brilliance, noted writer Venkatesh Madgulkar had once remarked: “Had ‘Balkavi’ (the pen name of nature poet Tryambak Bapu Thombre) tried to write prose, then it would have been like Shrinivas Kulkarni’s work.”Born on Nov 20, 1936, in Audumbar, Kulkarni completed his primary education in the village and later studied at Ankalkhop and Sangli. After working briefly as a signboard painter and in a glass factory, he joined Mouj publication and went on to edit the influential literary magazine for several years, nurturing generations of Marathi writers.Though he began his literary journey as a poet, writing his first poem while studying in Class IV, Kulkarni eventually found his true calling in prose.His first essay, ‘Manatlya Unhat’, was published in ‘Satyakatha’ in 1960, marking the beginning of a celebrated writing career.His major prose collections include ‘Doh’ (1965), ‘Sonyacha Pimpal’ (1975), ‘Panyache Pankh’ (1987) and ‘Kordi Bhiksha’ (2000), all of which were first published in ‘Satyakatha’ and ‘Mouj’ before being compiled into books.Earlier this year, Maharashtra govt announced the Vinda Karandikar Lifetime Achievement Award for Kulkarni.Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis condoled his death, stating: “With his demise, we have lost a steadfast, sensitive figure from the Marathi literary world. Through ‘Mouj’, he provided a platform to numerous emerging writers, he gave a new direction to the Marathi literary world. With his passing, we have lost a dedicated, inspirational figure who served Marathi literature with steadfastness.”Former chief minister Prithviraj Chavan said, “In passing of Shrinivas Kulkarni, Maharashtra has lost someone who dedicated for making Marathi literature rich. As a resident of Karad town, we were very proud to have Kulkarni as a resident of the town.”
Article Summary: Shrinivas Vinayak Kulkarni, popularly known as ‘Shrivi’, passed away at Karad on Thursday following a prolonged illness. He is survived by his wife, two sons, daughters-in-law and grandchildren. Widely acclaimed for his landmark work ‘Doh, Kulkar brought to life the landscape, people and memories of Audumbar, his village in Sangli district, on the banks of Krishna river.

Article Title: 4 held for theft of 17 kg silver mask, cladding of Shivling at historic temple in Maharashtra's Khopoli

NAVI MUMBAI: The Khopoli police in Raigad detected the burglary at the 18th century historic Shree Vireshwar temple, where 17 kg silver mask and silver cladding on Shivling was stolen on July 19 past midnight around 2 am, by arresting four accused burglars on Tuesday.The arrested accused are Amol Kasbe (36) and Vikas Agiwale (25), who were arrested from Shirur, Pune district and Dilip Jadhav (40) and Sakharam Gaikwad (40), who were arrested from Parner in Ahilyanagar district.The 17 kg silver mask and cladding on the Shivling was adorned in 2023 for which the around Rs 28 lakhs expenses were borne by the temple's trust from the donations received from devotees.Sachin Hire, senior inspector of Khopoli said, "On July 19, the assistant priest at the temple identified as Kishore Shigwan (56) lodge a complaint that the silver mask and cladding on Shivling was stolen. The thieves had entered the temple by breaking the chain and lock of the rear gate, which always remained close as the devotees were allowed entry only from the front gate.""Upon checking CCTV camera footage at the temple, it was seen that four masked men had entered the sanctum sanctorum around 2 am and decamped with the silver mask and cladding on the Shivling. Subsequently, an FIR was registered under BNS sections for house tres-pass, theft in a dwelling house and joint criminal liability. "Inspector Hire said, "Multiple teams were formed to trace the gang of burglars.Using technical expertise and informer network, we zeroed-in on four history-sheeters. They were traced to Pune and Ahilyanagar district and gradually apprehended on Tuesday.""They have revealed the place where they have hidden the stolen silver mask and cladding. Accordingly, a police team will recover the stolen valuables. Previously, there are criminal cases of theft and robbery registered against the arrested accused in Ahilyanagar and Pune districts."

On the signal of the customer customer, we raided the lodge, where 9 women were kept for prostitution. The lodge manager Balram Gowda, waiters Girish Pujari and Krishnaraj Patil were arrested for dragging the women into prostitution. An FIR was registered at Taloja police station against the three arrested accused Gowda, Pujari and Patil, who were booked relevant BNS sections and Prevention of Immoral Trafficking Act. The Panvel court remanded them to police custody till July 21. The rescued women were sent to women's shelter home as directed by the magistrate."
Article Summary: The Anti-Human Trafficking Unit of Navi Mumbai crime branch busted a prostitution racket at hotel-cum lodge in Taloja. The crime branch team arrested three accused including the lodge manager and two waiters. The lodge manager Balram Gowda, waiters Girish Pujari and Krishnaraj Patil were arrested.

Article Title: Truck driver arrested from Gujarat for killing fellow driver with iron rod over caste dispute in Maharashtra
Article Text:
Taloja police have caught a truck driver involved in the tragic murder of a fellow driver during a dispute fueled by caste discrimination (Representative image)

NAVI MUMBAI: Taloja police have arrested a 40-year-old truck driver who had absconded after fatally assaulting a 45-year-old truck driver on his head with an iron rod in the truck parking lot of Nisha Transport company in Nitlas village near Taloja industrial area in Panvel taluka on July 14 early morning.The accused was arrested from Valsad railway station, Gujarat on Friday, while he was escaping by train to his home town in UP.The arrested accused has been identified as Ramesh Kumar Yadav and the murder victim as Chandan Pandey, both hailing from UP.Sagar Nikam, PI (crime) of Taloja said, "The murder was an outcome of the Pandey versus Yadav caste discrimination, especially in UP. The accused Yadav had fatally assaulted the victim Pandey as the latter being a Brahmin used to humiliate Yadav from OBC by treating him as inferior, as claimed by the accused Yadav."PI Nikam informed, "On Monday night, an argument has ensued between Pandey and Yadav in the parking lot over caste discrimination. As they quarrelled, the other truck drivers intervened and resolved the matter. On Tuesday around 5.30 am, again both of them quarrelled, when Yadav assaulted on Pandey's head with an iron rod that proved fatal.""Pandey escaped after threatening other truckers if they attempted to catch him. The security guard Mohammad Alam Hajif-ul Khan (58) informed the police. Pandey was rushed to Panvel sub-district hospital where he was declared brought dead. Subsequently, a murder case was registered against the accused Yadav. His photograph found in his parked truck was immediately circulated to the GRP and RPF at railway stations where multiple trains heading to UP halt.""On Friday, the Valsad GRP informed us that Yadav has been detained at Valsad railway station while he was travelling in an express train to escape to his hometown in UP. Our police team reached Valsad and arrested Yadav. The Panvel JMFC court has remanded Yadav to police custody untill July 21."
Article Summary: Ramesh Kumar Yadav, 40, was arrested from Valsad railway station, Gujarat on Friday. He had absconded after fatally assaulting a 45-year-old truck driver on his head with an iron rod. The murder was an outcome of the Pandey versus Yadav caste discrimination, especially in UP.

Article Title: Thane doctors remove rare 8.5-kg abdominal tumour from 20-year-old woman after complex surgery
Article Text:
Doctors successfully removed a rare 8.5-kilogram abdominal tumor from a young woman





THANE: Doctors at the Thane Municipal Corporation-run Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Hospital in Kalwa removed a rare 8.5-kg abdominal tumour from a 20-year-old woman, following a complex surgery.The patient had been complaining of pain and swelling on the left side of her abdomen for the past six months.Subsequent investigations revealed a large mass occupying the left side of her abdomen and extending from the pelvic region to the upper abdomen.“A CT scan showed the tumour measured around 1.5 feet in length and 1 foot in width. Fortunately, it had not affected any other organs, though it had slightly displaced their positions. Nonetheless, our team decided to operate on her and removed the tumour successfully despite its complex location,” said hospital Dean Dr. Swapnali Kadam.The surgery was performed by Dr. Varsha Patil, Dr. Kshitij Mane and Dr. Shubham More under the guidance of Dr. Arun Mane, head of the surgery department.The anaesthesia team comprising Dr. Vijay Patil, Dr. Ketaki Patwardhan and Dr. Sanjana Patil also played a key role in the procedure.The patient, who was kept under observation after the surgery conducted last month, has shown significant improvement.Her weight has reduced by around 6-7 kg following the removal of the tumour, said hospital Superintendent Dr. Aniruddha Malgaonkar.“The procedure was challenging as tumours of such a large size in the retroperitoneal region, the deep area behind organs such as the kidneys and pancreas, are extremely rare.Surgeries in this region are particularly difficult due to the presence of major blood vessels and other vital organs,” Dr. Kadam said.The removed tumour has been sent for histopathological examination, and doctors are awaiting the report to determine its exact nature.
Article Summary: The patient had been complaining of pain and swelling on the left side of her abdomen for the past six months. CT scan showed the tumour measured around 1.5 feet in length and 1 foot in width. Fortunately, it had not affected any other organs, though it had slightly displaced their positions.

Article Title: After poll debut in 2024, Niwara residents face SIR mapping challenge
Article Text:
Senior citizens in Niwara old age home face SIR mapping challenge

Pune:

TOI

TOI





Suman Govekar, an 84-year-old member of Niwara old-age home, was very excited when she exercised her voting rights in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, after getting her name enrolled in the electoral list. Two years on, she is struggling in relative-mapping or progeny for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). She does not have any documents.There are 117 senior citizens, including Govekar, in Niwara — Pune’s oldest old-age home. Their names are in the voters’ list. But away from their families and homes for years, they do not have documents to submit for their relatives’ mapping in the ongoing SIR exercise.A couple of years ago, they did not even have their names enrolled in the voters’ list. They did not have any documents to submit as a residential proof.Vijay Belsare, the secretary of Niwara, told, “The trust took initiative and got an Aadhaar card for each member by showing the old-age home as their residence. Based on the Aadhaar number, their names could be enrolled in the voters’ list. Most of them exercised their right to vote for the first time in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls. Now we are worried that their names might be deleted as they do not have any documents to prove their relatives’ mapping.”Chitra Dhopate (71) has been living at Niwara for several years. She does not have any document other than the voting card with her.“Ever since I came to the old-age home, I did not have any identity proof. When I got my voter identity card, I was very happy that I got some document of my own. Beyond the voter card, I do not have any document which has my name on it,” Dhopate toldDuring the ongoing SIR exercise, the trustees helped these members to fill up the forms and submitted them to the booth-level officer (BLO) for further process. Belsare said, “Most of these members have been staying here for the past few decades with no connection with their families. Many of them do not even remember their past clearly. In such a situation, getting details of their relatives for mapping is next to impossible. ”Belsare added, “When they got their voters’ card, they got a sense of belonging after seeing their names and photos on a govt document. Now, we are trying to approach the administrative officials and request them to consider these senior citizens as a special case and ensure their names stay in the voters’ list.”Electoral registration officer (ERO) Vitthal Udamale said, “We will consider their request and if the need arises, we will make special arrangements. Our officers will visit the old-age home to conduct a hearing for every member.”
Article Summary: There are 117 senior citizens in Niwara — Pune’s oldest old-age home. Their names are in the voters’ list. But away from their families and homes for years, they do not have documents to submit for their relatives’ mapping.
